symbols.name: m
symbols.role: fixed number of individuals observed in each cluster

symbols.name: mu
symbols.role: unknown mixing law of latent cluster environments

symbols.name: ell
symbols.role: generic lower count-measurable envelope with Bernstein coefficient vector \(\ell=(\ell_c)_c\)

symbols.name: u
symbols.role: generic upper count-measurable envelope with Bernstein coefficient vector \(u=(u_c)_c\)

symbols.name: E_m
symbols.type: class of valid degree-\(m\) count-measurable envelope pairs
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_m=\{(\ell,u)\in V_m^2:\ell(q)\le f(q)\le u(q)\text{ for every }q\in K_{\epsilon}\}\)

symbols.name: M_hscm
symbols.type: class of hierarchical structural causal models
symbols.role: positive fixed-plate hierarchical SCM class defined in Definition 1

symbols.name: p_star
symbols.role: reference propensity in the limited-pooling comparator

symbols.name: z_obs
symbols.role: realized value of the aggregate count vector

symbols.name: T_n
symbols.def: \(T_n(z;b')=2\sum_{c:z_c>0}z_c\log\{z_c/(nb'_c)\}\), where a zero-count summand is \(0\) and \(T_n(z;b')=+\infty\) if \(z_c>0=b'_c\) for some \(c\)

symbols.name: P_n
symbols.def: \(P_n(b';z)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal H_n:T_n(w;b')\ge T_n(z;b')}\frac{n!}{\prod_cw_c!}\prod_c(b'_c)^{w_c}\), with every deviance tie included in the upper tail

symbols.name: R_n_alpha
symbols.type: confidence region for the count law
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_{n,\alpha}(z^{\mathrm{obs}})=\{b'\in\Delta_{N_m-1}:P_n(b';z^{\mathrm{obs}})>\alpha\}\); the test is nonrandomized, includes all deviance ties, and rejects exactly when \(P_n\le\alpha\)

symbols.name: C_n_alpha
symbols.type: confidence set for the entire identified interval

symbols.name: CAD_conf
symbols.role: procedure returning the semialgebraic ATE confidence set or its certified endpoint hull

symbols.name: CAD_m
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{CAD}_m(b,\epsilon)\) uses a relative-interior primal--dual contact branch and an arbitrary-boundary finite-support primal branch followed by a separate dual-certificate decision

symbols.name: A_boundary
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A_{m,\epsilon}\) is obtained by CAD stratification of faces of \(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\) together with tests of whether \(f\) is affine on each representing support variety

symbols.name: d_m
symbols.role: uniform distance from the causal integrand to the degree-\(m\) Bernstein span on the overlap-restricted simplex

assumptions.condition: \((Q_i,(A_{ij},Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1))_{j=1}^m)\) are independent and identically distributed across \(i\).
Conditional on \(Q_i=q\), the vectors \((A_{ij},Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1))\) are identically distributed and mutually independent over \(j\).
\(\Pr((A_{ij},Y_{ij})=(a,y)\mid Q_i)=Q_{i,ay}\) almost surely for every \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\), \(1\le i\le n\), and \(1\le j\le m\).

definitions.name: Positive fixed-plate hierarchical SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}=\{(\mu,\mathcal M):\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon}),\ Q_i\sim\mu,\ (Q_i,(A_{ij},Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1))_{j=1}^m)_{i=1}^n\text{ satisfies independent cluster sampling, conditional iid sampling, observed-cell calibration, latent ignorability, and consistency}\}\)

definitions.name: Bernstein majorant--minorant dual
definitions.construction: \(D_m(b)=(\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{N_m}}\{\lambda^\top b:\sum_c\lambda_cB_c^{(m)}\le f\text{ on }K_{\epsilon}\},\inf_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{N_m}}\{\lambda^\top b:\sum_c\lambda_cB_c^{(m)}\ge f\text{ on }K_{\epsilon}\})\)

definitions.name: Valid degree-\(m\) count-measurable envelope class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_m=\{(\ell,u)\in V_m^2:\ell(q)\le f(q)\le u(q)\text{ for every }q\in K_{\epsilon}\}\), where \(\ell^\top b=\sum_c\ell_cb_c\) and \(u^\top b=\sum_cu_cb_c\) use the unique degree-\(m\) Bernstein coefficient vectors

definitions.name: Best homogeneous order-m limited-pooling intersection
definitions.construction: For \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\) and \(p_*\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), set \(I_{LW,m,p_*}(b)=[\ell_{m,p_*}^{\top}b,u_{m,p_*}^{\top}b]\) and define the best homogeneous scalar-reference intersection by \(I_{LW,m}^{\cap}(b)=[\max_{p_*\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]}\ell_{m,p_*}^{\top}b,\min_{p_*\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]}u_{m,p_*}^{\top}b]\), where the dot products use the unique degree-\(m\) Bernstein coefficient vectors of \(\ell_{m,p_*},u_{m,p_*}\in V_m\)

definitions.name: Exact multinomial likelihood-inversion region
definitions.construction: For observed \(z^{\mathrm{obs}}\in\mathcal H_n\), enumerate every \(w\in\mathcal H_n\), compute the exact multinomial upper-tail probability \(P_n(b';z^{\mathrm{obs}})\) using \(T_n(w;b')\ge T_n(z^{\mathrm{obs}};b')\), include every deviance tie, use no auxiliary randomization, and retain \(b'\) exactly when \(P_n(b';z^{\mathrm{obs}})>\alpha\)

definitions.name: Finite-complexity ATE confidence-set recovery
definitions.construction: Represent \(t\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(z^{\mathrm{obs}})\) by variables \(b'\), \(1\le s\le N_m+1\), atom locations \(q^1,\ldots,q^s\in K_{\epsilon}\), and masses \(\omega_k\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_k\omega_k=1\), \(b'_c=\sum_k\omega_kB_c^{(m)}(q^k)\) for every \(c\), \(t=\sum_k\omega_k f(q^k)\), and \(b'\in\mathcal R_{n,\alpha}(z^{\mathrm{obs}})\); split by the finitely many deviance-order cells, clear positive propensity denominators, and apply CAD to eliminate all variables except \(t\)

definitions.name: Finite-support CAD recovery procedure
definitions.construction: Use two quantified branches. On the relative-interior branch, use at most \(N_m\) atoms, impose the rational simplex, overlap, mass, Bernstein-moment, objective, global dual-feasibility, and complementary-contact conditions, clear only the positive factors \(p(q)(1-p(q))\), and return algebraic primal endpoints, endpoint atoms, and matching dual certificates. On the arbitrary rational boundary branch, use at most \(N_m\) atoms and optimize the finite-support primal endpoint formula without any dual variables; after returning both algebraic primal endpoints and endpoint atoms, separately decide existence of matching global dual certificates. If no matching certificate exists, return a boundary/nonattainment flag rather than declaring the primal infeasible or withholding its endpoints and witnesses

definitions.name: Boundary fiber atlas handle
definitions.construction: Stratify the semialgebraic faces of \(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\) by CAD and, on each representing support variety, test membership of the restricted function \(f\) in the affine span of the restricted Bernstein coordinates

statements.statement: Every \((\mu,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\) has \(Q_i\sim\mu\), conditional count law \(C_i\mid Q_i=q\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}(m,q)\), marginal count law \(\Pr(C_i=c)=\int B_c^{(m)}(q)\,d\mu(q)\), and cluster-equally-weighted ATE \(\tau(\mu)=\int\{q_{11}/p(q)-q_{01}/(1-p(q))\}\,d\mu(q)=\int f\,d\mu\). Conversely, for every \(\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\), draw \(Q_i\sim\mu\); conditional on \(Q_i=q\), draw \(A_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p(q))\) and conditionally treatment-independent binary potential outcomes \(Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1)\) with means \(q_{01}/(1-p(q))\) and \(q_{11}/p(q)\), respectively, independently over \(j\), and set \(Y_{ij}=A_{ij}Y_{ij}(1)+(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}(0)\). This construction belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\) and has conditional cell probabilities \(\Pr((A_{ij},Y_{ij})=(a,y)\mid Q_i)=Q_{i,ay}\) almost surely.
statements.justification: This establishes that the moment program is exactly the compatible hierarchical SCM problem rather than a relaxation.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. construct finite response-type programs, while this lemma reconstructs a continuous-latent hierarchical SCM from every feasible mixing measure.
statements.consumer: It lets an applied analyst interpret every reported endpoint as an attainable data-generating process for the São Paulo city hierarchy.

statements.statement:
Let \(H_{m,\epsilon}:=\operatorname{conv}\{(g_m(q),f(q)):q\in K_{\epsilon}\}\). The set \(H_{m,\epsilon}\) is compact and equals
\[
 \left\{\left(\int g_m\,d\nu,\int f\,d\nu\right):
 \nu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\right\}.
\]
Every pair in \(H_{m,\epsilon}\) has a representing probability measure supported on at most \(N_m+1\) points of \(K_{\epsilon}\), and therefore has a compatible hierarchical SCM in \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\) with at most \(N_m+1\) latent cluster laws. Consequently, for every \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\), the sharp fiber \(\Theta_{m,\epsilon}(b)\) is a nonempty attained compact interval \([L_m(b),U_m(b)]\), and each endpoint has a representing measure, and hence a compatible hierarchical SCM, supported on at most \(N_m={m+3\choose3}\) latent laws. If \(b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\), then \(D_m(b)=(L_m(b),U_m(b))\) with both dual extrema attained. If an optimal dual polynomial has contact image of affine dimension \(r\), its associated endpoint admits at most \(r+1\) atoms.
statements.justification: The theorem supplies the all-feasible sharp causal fiber, the all-feasible \(N_m\)-atom endpoint SCM compression, and an attained evaluable dual on the relative interior.
statements.gap: General moment duality and cubature results do not derive the hierarchical causal hull, prove that its vertical endpoint faces compress to \(N_m\) atoms for every feasible count law, or supply the relative-interior Bernstein dual with compatible SCM semantics.
statements.consumer: It replaces random-effect specification sensitivity in the DOT analysis with the smallest ATE interval implied by the count law and overlap, plus compatible endpoint models using at most \(N_m\) latent laws even on the boundary.

statements.justification: This is the missing bridge from mixing-law nonuniqueness to strict variation of the particular causal functional on every interior fiber.
statements.gap: Halaseh et al. supply the full-support representative, but not the residual perturbation that separates a nonlinear causal functional while preserving all observed Bernstein moments.
statements.consumer: It certifies that reporting a point ATE for any interior fixed-plate count law necessarily uses structure beyond latent ignorability and overlap.

statements.statement: For every finite \(m\ge1\) and every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), \(V_m\) is the restriction to \(K_{\epsilon}\) of polynomials of total degree at most \(m\) on the simplex, whereas \(f(q)=q_{11}/p(q)-q_{01}/(1-p(q))\) does not belong to \(V_m\).
statements.justification: The rational propensity denominators are the exact component hidden by every finite Bernstein plate.
statements.gap: Wood establishes finite-moment aliasing of the mixing law, but does not test membership of this four-cell ATE functional in the observable function span.
statements.consumer: This gives a model-free diagnosis of why increasing the number of clusters cannot restore point identification when the within-cluster plate remains fixed.

statements.statement: For a continuous functional \(h:K_{\epsilon}\to\mathbb R\), \(\int h\,d\nu\) is identical for all \(\nu\in\mathcal F_{m,\epsilon}(b)\) and every feasible \(b\) if and only if \(h\in V_m\). For \(h=f\), universal point identification therefore fails for every finite \(m\), and every \(b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\) satisfies \(L_m(b)<U_m(b)\).
statements.justification: The iff condition separates recoverability of a target functional from recoverability of the entire mixing law and yields a robust nonidentification region.
statements.gap: Wood and Basu et al. prove mixing-distribution nonidentification under bounded plates; they do not give a necessary-and-sufficient span criterion or strict ATE width at every interior law.
statements.consumer: Investigators can determine whether a proposed hierarchical estimand is learned by fixed plate data by checking one finite-dimensional span condition.

statements.statement: For \(m\ge2\) and any \(q^*\in K_{\epsilon}\), the boundary moment vector \(b=g_m(q^*)\) has \(\mathcal F_{m,\epsilon}(b)=\{\delta_{q^*}\}\) and hence \(L_m(b)=U_m(b)=f(q^*)\).
statements.justification: The second Bernstein moments force zero latent variance and show exactly why the relative-interior restriction cannot be dropped.
statements.gap: General mixture nonidentification statements do not record that fixed-plate causal fibers can collapse on exposed boundary images.
statements.consumer: The proposition prevents confidence procedures and empirical diagnostics from treating near-boundary laws as uniformly wide partially identified cases.

statements.statement: For every \((\ell,u)\in\mathcal E_m\) and every \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\), \([L_m(b),U_m(b)]\subseteq[\ell^\top b,u^\top b]\). The lower equality \(L_m(b)=\ell^\top b\) holds if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{conv}\{g_m(q):q\in K_{\epsilon},\ \ell(q)=f(q)\}\), and the upper equality \(U_m(b)=u^\top b\) holds if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{conv}\{g_m(q):q\in K_{\epsilon},\ u(q)=f(q)\}\). If \(m\ge2\), each contact hull is a proper closed convex subset of \(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\); consequently, for each endpoint separately there is a nonempty relatively open subset of \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\) on which the sharp endpoint strictly improves its valid envelope endpoint.
statements.justification: The contact-hull criterion identifies exactly where any valid degree-\(m\) count-measurable bound is already sharp and where optimizing the complete moment fiber must improve it.
statements.gap: Published limited-pooling bounds provide particular valid polynomial envelopes, but do not give a generic sharp-envelope domination theorem or an exact contact-hull equality criterion for the complete count law.
statements.consumer: An analyst can test a proposed count-measurable ATE envelope by computing its contact hull and can localize observable laws where the sharp fiber yields a strict gain.

statements.statement: For rational \(\epsilon\) and rational \(b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\), the relative-interior branch of \(\operatorname{CAD}_m(b,\epsilon)\) terminates and returns the algebraic numbers \(L_m(b)\) and \(U_m(b)\) by minimal polynomials and isolating intervals, endpoint measures with at most \(N_m\) atoms, compatible endpoint models in \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\), and matching globally feasible Bernstein dual certificates. For arbitrary rational \(b\), the boundary-capable branch first decides primal feasibility using no dual variables. If \(b\notin\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\), it certifies infeasibility. If \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\), it terminates and returns both algebraic primal endpoints, endpoint measures with at most \(N_m\) atoms, and compatible endpoint models, then separately decides whether matching globally feasible dual certificates exist; absence of a matching certificate returns a boundary/nonattainment flag and does not alter the primal endpoints or witnesses.
statements.justification: The theorem converts each infinite-dimensional endpoint problem into a terminating exact certificate with an all-feasible \(N_m\)-atom witness.
statements.gap: Symbolic bounds for finite response-function models and generic CAD do not cover an unrestricted Borel mixing law, rational Bernstein-fiber ATE endpoints, the all-feasible \(N_m\)-atom endpoint reduction, or exact compatible-SCM witness recovery.
statements.consumer: Applied analyses can report reproducible algebraic endpoints and \(N_m\)-atom compatible witnesses for interior or boundary count laws, independently of optimizer choices.

statements.statement: For fixed \(m,n\), observed \(z^{\mathrm{obs}}\in\mathcal H_n\), and \(0<\alpha<1\), the nonrandomized likelihood-ratio test that rejects \(b'\) when \(P_n(b';z^{\mathrm{obs}})\le\alpha\), with every equality \(T_n(w;b')=T_n(z^{\mathrm{obs}};b')\) included in the upper tail, has rejection probability at most \(\alpha\) under \(Z\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}(n,b')\). Its inversion \(\mathcal R_{n,\alpha}(z^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is semialgebraic: on each zero-pattern cell, every deviance comparison is equivalent after exponentiation and positive-denominator clearing to a monomial polynomial inequality, and \(P_n\) is a finite polynomial sum. If \(\epsilon\), \(\alpha\), and \(z^{\mathrm{obs}}\) are rational, then \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(z^{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq[-1,1]\) is a one-dimensional semialgebraic set. The procedure \(\operatorname{CAD}^{\mathrm{conf}}_{m,n}\) terminates after reducing each feasible \((b',t)\) to at most \(N_m+1\) atoms and returns either the complete disjoint decomposition into points and intervals with every algebraic endpoint and open-or-closed endpoint flag, or the certified endpoint hull with its attainability flags.
statements.justification: The theorem makes exact finite-sample inversion a finite real-algebraic computation rather than an abstract union over count laws and mixing measures.
statements.gap: Sachs, Jonzon, Sjölander, and Gabriel derive tight symbolic bounds by linear programming and vertex enumeration for finite response-function causal models, while Basu, Brill, and Yekutieli invert exact tests for particular univariate mixing functionals.  Neither treats the unrestricted Borel four-cell mixing law, rational Bernstein ATE fiber, finite-atom reduction, and exact semialgebraic whole-set inversion proved here.
statements.consumer: For fixed rational inputs, the São Paulo analysis has an in-principle exact decomposition or certified endpoint hull, without any asserted practical runtime.

statements.statement: Corollary. For every \(n,m\), every \(0<\alpha<1\), and every \((\mu,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\) with true count law \(b\), exact count-law coverage gives \(\Pr_{\mathcal M}(b\in\mathcal R_{n,\alpha}(Z))\ge1-\alpha\). On this event, the defining union for \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(Z)\) contains \([L_m(b),U_m(b)]\); hence \(\Pr_{\mathcal M}([L_m(b),U_m(b)]\subseteq\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(Z))\ge1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\), including boundary laws with singleton fibers.
statements.justification: This corollary is solely the exact count-law coverage event combined with the defining union for the ATE confidence set.
statements.gap: The inference contribution is computational semialgebraicity and exact recovery; the coverage statement records the resulting finite-sample guarantee without presenting it as a separate difficult theorem.
statements.consumer: Analysts obtain uniform coverage of the full nonparametric ATE fiber even near point-identified faces.

statements.statement: When \(m=1\), \(\epsilon=1/4\), and \(b=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), the exact sharp interval is \([-1/3,1/3]\). The upper dual certificate is \(1-\frac43(q_{01}+q_{10})\), the lower certificate is \(\frac13-\frac43(q_{01}+q_{10})\), and each endpoint is attained by a mixing law with at most four atoms.
statements.justification: The closed-form base case checks the signs, overlap convention, dual orientation, and support cap.
statements.gap: Published binomial-mixture examples do not give this four-cell causal ATE regression case.
statements.consumer: The example is a unit test for symbolic implementations and a transparent teaching case for fixed-plate causal nonidentification.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathcal A_{m,\epsilon}\) be completed into a finite semialgebraic stratification of \(\operatorname{relbd}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\), taken in \(\operatorname{aff}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\), such that each stratum records whether \(L_m(b)=U_m(b)\), the affine dimension of the ATE image, and the smallest lower- and upper-endpoint support sizes?
statements.justification: The question isolates classification of exceptional relative-boundary fibers and the minimum complexity of their lower- and upper-endpoint witnesses.
statements.gap: Neither truncated-moment geometry nor symbolic causal-bound work classifies relative-boundary fibers on which a nonlinear causal target becomes accidentally constant while also recording endpoint support minima.
statements.consumer: Its resolution lets an analyst distinguish data-driven boundary precision from parametric regularization and recover minimum-support endpoint witnesses.

sampling_model.design: Observational hierarchical sampling with a fixed plate of \(m\) individuals per cluster.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) clusters are independent draws; conditional on \(Q_i\), the \(m\) individual causal vectors are iid.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is binary and conditionally ignorable given \(Q_i\); because \(Q_i\in K_{\epsilon}\), its cluster-specific probability \(p(Q_i)\) lies in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\).
sampling_model.observed_data: Only \(C_i\), the four-cell multinomial count of \((A,Y)\) within cluster \(i\), is observed.
sampling_model.latent_structure: Every class member contains \(\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\), draws \(Q_i\sim\mu\), and satisfies \(\Pr((A_{ij},Y_{ij})=(a,y)\mid Q_i)=Q_{i,ay}\) almost surely for every cell and individual.
sampling_model.overlap: Overlap is encoded by the declared spaces \(\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\) and \(Q_i\in K_{\epsilon}\), not by a separate support assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite-dimensional observable nuisance is the multinomial count law \(b\), estimated by \(\widehat b\); the mixing law is not estimated pointwise.

estimand_functional: \(\Theta_{m,\epsilon}(b)=[L_m(b),U_m(b)]\) for every \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\); if \(b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\), this interval also equals \(\left[\max_{\lambda:\sum_c\lambda_cB_c^{(m)}\leq f}\lambda^\top b,\min_{\lambda:\sum_c\lambda_cB_c^{(m)}\geq f}\lambda^\top b\right]\), with both extrema attained. For \(d_m(\epsilon)\) as explicitly defined in Definition \texttt{def:uniform-identification-modulus}, \(\max_{b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}}\{U_m(b)-L_m(b)\}=\sup_{b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})}\{U_m(b)-L_m(b)\}=2d_m(\epsilon)\). Writing \(\rho=1-2\epsilon\), the shifted-Chebyshev construction gives \(0<d_m(\epsilon)\leq\operatorname{sech}(m\operatorname{arcosh}(1/\rho))\leq\rho^m\), with the last inequality strict for \(m\geq2\). Thus every feasible width is at most \(2\operatorname{sech}(m\operatorname{arcosh}(1/(1-2\epsilon)))\), without claiming equality between the modulus and this upper bound or an exact asymptotic.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed binomial size, the observable mixture determines only finitely many moments and interior observable laws generally have nonunique mixing representations.
Binomial-mixture membership is equivalent to infinite extendibility for the associated finite exchangeable Bernoulli law.

Lee and Weidner analyze an observed-\(X\) conditional-factorization class that may allow continuous or discrete \(X\). Only their pointwise population envelope transfers to the latent-\(Q\) count experiment: the intersection over all scalar references \(p_*\) of the explicitly defined homogeneous, constant-coefficient order-\(m\), count-law-only envelope pair is valid, but the sharp cluster-count fiber is strictly tighter at both endpoints simultaneously on a nonempty relatively open interior region. Their estimator and asymptotic theory do not transfer and are not compared.
Interior moment vectors yield strong duality for generalized moment problems.
Relative-interior compact polynomial moment data admit dual attainment and full-support representing measures.

Winkler's Theorem 2.1(b), with its usual linear-independence characterization of support-point constraint vectors, implies the finite-support bound for extreme generalized-moment measures; support size alone does not characterize extremality.
A finite function system admits an integral-preserving atomic cubature rule with support bounded by its dimension.
Finite discrete SCM bounds can be computed by polynomial optimization with numerical valid and epsilon-sharp certificates.

Tight symbolic bounds for categorical causal DAGs are derived by linear programming and vertex enumeration after finite response-function reduction, with linear observed-probability constraints and a linear causal query.
Bootstrap inversion can control coverage of an entire identified set defined by finitely many moment inequalities.
Exact test inversion yields pointwise confidence intervals for CDFs and quantiles of an unrestricted binomial mixing law.

tldr: Fixed-size cluster counts reveal only degree-\(m\) Bernstein moments of latent four-cell exposure--outcome laws, so the cluster-equally-weighted ATE is an interval rather than a point. Each hierarchical SCM carries \(\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\), draws \(Q_i\sim\mu\), and calibrates the observed four-cell law to \(Q_i\). The sharp interval has attained measure and Bernstein-polynomial programs for every relative-interior count law, with compatible endpoint SCMs using at most \({m+3\choose3}\) latent laws. A generic contact-hull theorem exactly characterizes equality with any valid degree-\(m\) count-measurable envelope and gives strict improvement regions, while exact multinomial likelihood inversion produces a semialgebraic ATE confidence set recoverable by terminating CAD.

project_justification.gap: The São Paulo DOT analysis shows that city random-effect choices move the posterior ATE, while fixed-plate mixture theory establishes finite-moment information loss without characterizing this causal functional. Existing limited-pooling ATE bounds use particular valid polynomials, and generalized-moment theory lacks the hierarchical SCM semantics and strict-fiber conclusion.
project_justification.niche: The observable cluster-count law is finite dimensional, but the latent city law is unrestricted and the causal target is a nonlinear reciprocal functional. This creates a tractable convex moment geometry whose causal identified set has not been characterized.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the sharp primal--dual interval, proves an iff Bernstein-span identification frontier and strict width throughout the relative interior, constructs finite-latent endpoint SCMs, gives an exact contact-hull criterion and strict improvement regions for every valid degree-\(m\) envelope with Lee--Weidner as a corollary, and turns exact multinomial inversion into a one-dimensional semialgebraic confidence set with terminating CAD recovery.

related_work: Nobre, Schmidt, Moodie, and Stephens (2023, Sections 5--6 and Figure 3) motivate the problem by documenting ATE sensitivity to city random effects in the São Paulo DOT study. Wood (1999, Introduction and Sections 2--4, especially Example 2 on pp. 1717--1718) develops fixed-binomial convex geometry and exhibits a polygonal nonidentifiable slice but does not study a four-cell causal functional. Wood (1992, p. 1167) connects binomial-mixture membership to infinite extendibility of a finite exchangeable Bernoulli law; this is background for the repeated-observation interpretation, not a causal-functional comparator. Rosenbaum and Rubin (1983) provide the standard conditional-ignorability framework and Rubin (1974) the potential-outcome framework underlying consistency; here ignorability is imposed conditional on latent \(Q_i\), and these assumptions are used in lem:scm-moment-reduction to map calibrated observed cells to the causal integrand. Lee and Weidner (2026, Section 4.2 and Proposition 2) are provenance only for the explicitly defined scalar-reference, count-law-only transplant, whose validity is proved directly from the displayed formulas; Section 5 and Theorem 3 give their associated fixed-order sample construction and asymptotic inference. This is not a comparison with their full covariate-dependent procedure. Bertsimas and Popescu (2005, Theorem 2.2) and Halaseh, Magron, and Skomra (2026, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 5.9) inform the strong-duality and full-support arguments. Bayer and Teichmann (2006, Theorem 1) inform atomic compression, while the endpoint contact face yields the causal support cap. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjölander, and Gabriel (2023, Sections 2--4) derive tight symbolic bounds by linear programming and vertex enumeration for categorical causal DAGs after reducing latent influences to a finite response-function state space, with linear observed-probability constraints and a linear causal query. They do not treat an unrestricted Borel mixing law over a continuous four-cell simplex, Bernstein moment fibers with the rational ATE functional, the required finite-atom reduction, or CAD recovery of an exact-inversion confidence set. Duarte et al. (2023, Proposition 1 and Algorithm 1) compute numerical polynomial causal bounds for finite discrete SCMs; the present continuous-latent problem first requires endpoint compression and then exact quantifier elimination. England, Bradford, and Davenport (2020, Theorem 1 and Algorithm 1) supply the CAD machinery. Bugni (2010, Theorems 1--3) motivates whole-set coverage, while Basu, Brill, and Yekutieli (2026, Section 4) motivate exact finite-sample inversion; neither source proves that the inverted hierarchical ATE set is semialgebraic or CAD-recoverable.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(m=2\) presolve certificate remains outstanding. For the rational full-support benchmark \(b_2^*\), finite-grid primal and dual linear programs agree numerically at approximately \([-0.05998,0.05998]\) and use ten active atoms, but this is not an algebraic CAD certificate and is not evidence for the exact endpoint values. The proposal therefore retains exact \(m=2\) primal--dual recovery as part of the open boundary-atlas question and as a required implementation kill test.
honest_scope: The central identification theorems concern relative-interior count laws and fixed finite \(m\). The Dirac-fiber proposition records point-identified boundary images for \(m\ge2\), so strict width is not asserted on the boundary. Whole-set coverage is only the immediate corollary of exact count-law coverage and the defining confidence-set union, not an independent solve target. The exact \(m=1\), \(\epsilon=1/4\), uniform-count proposition is a sanity check. A complete boundary stratification and the exact \(m=2\) certificate remain open; growing or heterogeneous plate sizes belong to the two retained follow-on seeds rather than the present kernel.
